title: At Least 16 Epstein-Related Files Disappeared from DOJ Webpage, AP Reports
description_short: AP reported that at least 16 Epstein-related files vanished from the DOJ webpage, including an image showing Trump with Epstein, Melania Trump and Ghislaine Maxwell.
description_medium: The Associated Press reported that at least 16 files posted to the Justice Department’s public Epstein-records webpage were no longer available the following day. The missing items included artwork and a photograph showing Donald Trump, Jeffrey Epstein, Melania Trump and Ghislaine Maxwell among other pictures. AP said the government had given no explanation or public notice at the time of its report.
description_long: The Associated Press reported on December 20, 2025, that at least 16 files posted to the Justice Department’s public webpage for Epstein-related records were no longer accessible less than a day later. AP said the files were available Friday and absent by Saturday. Among them were images of paintings depicting nude women and a photograph arrangement in which one picture showed Donald Trump with Jeffrey Epstein, Melania Trump and Epstein associate Ghislaine Maxwell. The report describes a change to what visitors could access on the public webpage; it does not establish that the records were destroyed or removed from government custody. AP reported that the Justice Department had provided no explanation or public notice at that time. The available reporting does not identify a Trump statement promising release of these particular files, establish who removed them, or explain why they disappeared. The supported claim is therefore the quantified webpage change and the contents AP identified, without attributing responsibility or alleging that it disproved a specific Trump promise.

title: CNP List Compiler Says Its 1,011-Name Membership List Is Incomplete
description_short: A public compilation lists 1,011 Council for National Policy names from 1981–2020 and says it may cover fewer than half of the group’s members.
description_medium: A 1981 New York Times report described more than 50 conservatives convening the Council for National Policy as a new umbrella group they hoped would gain influence. A later TrumpFile compilation says it lists 1,011 names from 1981 through 2020 and may include fewer than half of the council’s members. Documented separately published a leaked September 2020 directory naming 426 members. These sources describe the group and incomplete lists; they do not establish Donald Trump’s membership or role.
description_long: A New York Times report published May 20, 1981, said more than 50 well-known conservatives had convened the Council for National Policy, a new umbrella group they hoped would gain influence. Decades later, the TrumpFile page linked in this record describes a compilation of 1,011 names covering 1981 through 2020 and cautions that it may include fewer than half of the council’s members. Documented published a separate leaked September 2020 membership directory naming 426 people. Those figures describe different lists and should not be combined into a count of total members. Neither the linked compilation nor the supplied material verifies Donald Trump’s membership, position or participation in a CNP activity, and a person’s appearance in a multi-decade list would not by itself prove a role in a specific policy. The supported subject is the council’s formation and the scope and limitations of publicly available membership lists. Unless a reliable record connects Trump to the organization, this should be reframed as CNP history or excluded from a Trump-specific claim.

title: Trump Order Directs Federal Agencies to Restrict Gender-Affirming Care for Minors
description_short: Executive Order 14187 directs federal agencies to restrict federal support and coverage for gender-affirming care for people under 19.
description_medium: On January 28, 2025, Trump signed Executive Order 14187, which defines “child” as a person under 19 and directs agencies to restrict federal support for specified gender-affirming treatments. Human Rights Watch says the order targets federal funding for institutions providing or researching care and calls for limits through federal health programs. The sources do not support the original claim that a complete nationwide criminal ban was enacted.
description_long: On January 28, 2025, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14187, titled “Protecting Children from Chemical and Surgical Mutilation.” The order defines a child as a person under 19 and describes puberty blockers, certain hormones and some surgical procedures as the care it seeks to restrict. It directs federal agencies to take steps involving grants and federal health programs, including TRICARE, and instructs the attorney general to prioritize enforcement of laws the order says prohibit or limit the procedures. Human Rights Watch’s June 2025 report describes the order as restricting federal funding for institutions that provide or research gender-affirming care and cutting off access through federal programs. These provisions support an account of the administration’s federal restrictions and policy direction. They do not establish that every form of care was eliminated nationwide, that providers were criminally prohibited from offering care, or that a complete federal ban had taken effect. The narrower title and description therefore identify the signed order and its stated directives without claiming universal implementation or consequences beyond the cited sources.

preserved_fields.title: Complete Gender-Affirming Care Ban - Federal Criminalization and Healthcare Elimination
preserved_fields.description_short: Complete Gender-Affirming Care Ban - Federal Criminalization and Healthcare Elimination
preserved_fields.description_long: Donald Trump implemented Project 2025's complete federal ban on gender-affirming care by criminalizing providers who offered transition-related treatment while classifying supportive parents and healthcare professionals as engaging in 'mutilation' and 'child abuse' despite evidence showing this care significantly reduced suicidality and provided long-term mental health benefits to transgender youth. The systematic healthcare criminalization represented Trump's expansion of 25 state-level bans affecting over 100,000 transgender youth to federal prohibition that eliminated access to puberty blockers and gender-affirming hormones associated with '60% lower odds of depression and 73% lower odds of suicide' over 12-month periods. The gender-affirming care elimination included directing CDC to stop collecting gender identity data while funding research into 'negative effects' of supportive care and exploring therapies aimed at convincing children they were not transgender, effectively ending medical support while promoting conversion practices that had been rejected by major medical organizations. Trump's healthcare targeting violated medical ethics and constitutional rights by overriding clinical judgment with political ideology while forcing healthcare providers to choose between evidence-based treatment supported by medical associations or compliance with federal criminalization that threatened imprisonment and career destruction. The care ban created what advocates called systematic elimination of lifesaving treatment that had enabled transgender youth to thrive while reducing mental health crises, transforming medical care from therapeutic intervention into criminal activity subject to prosecution and persecution. The complete gender-affirming care prohibition represented Project 2025's vision of healthcare controlled by conservative ideology rather than medical evidence, eliminating treatment that saved lives while forcing transgender Americans to seek care in other countries or face depression, anxiety, and suicide without supportive medical intervention.

title: Kari Lake Reinstated a Deferred-Resignation Offer for USAGM Employees
description_short: A court filing says Kari Lake reinstated a USAGM deferred-resignation program with a March 9, 2026, deadline and pay through September 5.
description_medium: A federal court filing states that Kari Lake reinstated a deferred-resignation program for U.S. Agency for Global Media employees in late February 2026. Staff could resign immediately and continue receiving pay through September 5, with a March 9 acceptance deadline. The filing said an earlier reduction-in-force was suspended by court order, while the agency still intended a significant RIF when able. The sources do not report program uptake or a measured service effect.
description_long: In late February 2026, Kari Lake reinstated a deferred-resignation program for employees of the U.S. Agency for Global Media (USAGM), the federal agency that oversees Voice of America and other international broadcasters. A court filing states that employees could resign immediately while continuing to receive pay through September 5, 2026, and had until March 9 to accept. The filing also quotes an agency message saying that an August 2025 reduction-in-force was suspended by court order, while USAGM still intended to carry out a significant reduction when it could. A federal judge later ruled that Lake had unlawfully served as acting head during much of 2025 and voided actions taken during that period, including mass-layoff measures. That ruling concerns Lake’s appointment and prior actions; the cited reports do not say how many employees accepted this deferred-resignation offer or measure any loss of broadcasting or national-security capability attributable to it. The evidence supports the offer, its terms and its staffing context, but not the original title’s claim that the program itself hurt national security.
